name: Dominica
rule: The Act requires permits and phytosanitary certification for restricted plant products, defined as processed or unprocessed material capable of carrying pests. Regulation 8(g) exempts cooked/parboiled/otherwise processed pest-free products from regulation 4 entry/declaration/inspection only; it does not expressly waive the Act’s permit/certificate provisions. SRO 8/2003 adds a fruit/vegetable/planting-material permit form, without classifying manufactured tea. ISPM32 Appendix2 expressly lists tea in Category1, but that standard excludes later contamination/storage pests and the inspected domestic1986 Act has no general mandatory ISPM-interpretation clause. No independent enacted private-parcel food certificate or special-approval duty was established; the2026 enacted-text/commencement retrieval gap is recorded separately rather than treated as a blocker.
personalMailApplicability: Individual import procedure exists; no personal postal tea exemption established.
remainingQuestion: How the domestic pest-capability definition applies to manufactured Category1 tea: Act2 covers material capable of harbouring or transporting plant pests, while ISPM32 excludes later contamination/storage pests from its scope. A general operative processing rule or published technical interpretation could settle this without a bespoke national tea ruling. No independent enacted food-document duty was established for the stated private parcel.
researchAttempts: Read the ministry import permit procedure, sample permit and Plant Protection Act. Preserved-fruit exceptions do not clearly cover manufactured Camellia tea; no personal postal waiver found.

30 September bounded legal-scope peer review: The parent Act defines processed and unprocessed plant products by capability of harbouring or transporting pests and directly requires prior permits with certificates for restricted articles. Regulation 8 expressly exempts listed articles only from regulation 4. Even if sencha qualified as cooked/processed and free of organisms under 8(g), that does not expressly waive Act sections 3–4. Being free of organisms in a given consignment is also a different proposition from being incapable of carrying pests as a product category. The complete subsidiary table names other crop controls but supplies no broader permit waiver for tea.
